text.original: وَالْحَادِي عَشَرَ اسْمُ لَا لِنَفْيِ الْجِنْسِ، نَحْوُ: لَا طَاعَةَ مُغْتَابٍ مَقْبُولَةٌ. وَالثَّانِي عَشَرَ خَبَرُ مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَيْنِ بِلَيْسَ، نَحْوُ: مَا الْغِيبَةُ حَلَالًا، وَلَا نَمِيمَةٌ جَائِزَةً. وَالثَّالِثَ عَشَرَ الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ الَّذِي دَخَلَهُ إِحْدَى النَّوَاصِبِ، نَحْوُ: أُحِبُّ أَنْ تُغْفَرَ ذُنُوبِي.
text.en: The eleventh is the noun of the lā that denies the whole kind, as lā ṭāʿata mughtābin maqbūlatun “no obedience of a backbiter is accepted”. The twelfth is the khabar of mā and lā that resemble laysa, as mā al-ghībatu ḥalālan “backbiting is not lawful” and wa-lā namīmatun jāʾizatan “and no tale-bearing is permitted”. The thirteenth is the muḍāriʿ verb on which one of the nawāṣib has come, as uḥibbu an tughfara dhunūbī “I love that my sins be forgiven”.

text.original: وَأَمَّا الْمَجْرُورُ فَاثْنَانِ: الْأَوَّلُ الْمَجْرُورُ بِحَرْفِ الْجَرِّ، نَحْوُ: اعْمَلْ بِإِخْلَاصٍ. وَالثَّانِي الْمَجْرُورُ بِالْإِضَافَةِ، نَحْوُ: ذَنْبُ الْعَبْدِ يُسَوِّدُ قَلْبَهُ. وَأَمَّا الْمَجْزُومُ فَوَاحِدٌ، وَهُوَ الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ الَّذِي دَخَلَهُ إِحْدَى الْجَوَازِمِ، نَحْوُ: إِنْ تُخْلِصْ يُقْبَلْ عَمَلُكَ.
text.en: As for the majrūr, it is two. The first is what is in jarr by a particle of jarr, as iʿmal bi-ikhlāṣin “act with sincerity”; the second is what is in jarr by iḍāfa, as dhanbu al-ʿabdi yusawwidu qalbahu “the servant's sin blackens his heart”. As for the majzūm, it is one: the muḍāriʿ verb on which one of the jawāzim has come, as in tukhliṣ yuqbal ʿamaluka “if you are sincere, your deed is accepted”.

lessons.title: The five followers
body: The governed words by following are five. The adjective (ṣifa): uʿbudi llāha al-ʿaẓīma, “worship God the Mighty”. The conjunction (ʿaṭf) with one of the ten particles, each with Birgivī's example: wa-, uṭīʿu llāha wa-l-rasūla, “I obey God and the Messenger”; fa-, tajibu takbīratu al-iftitāḥi fa-l-qiyāmu, “the opening takbīr is a duty, then the standing”; thumma, yajibu al-ʿilmu thumma al-ʿamalu, “knowledge is a duty, then action”; ḥattā, māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu, “people die, even the prophets”; aw, ṣalli al-ḍuḥā arbaʿan aw thamāniyan, “pray the forenoon prayer, four or eight”.

And immā: iʿmal immā wājiban wa-immā mustaḥabban, “do either what is obligatory or what is recommended”; am: a-riḍāʾa llāhi taṭlubu am sakhaṭahu?, “is it God's pleasure you seek, or His anger?”; lā: iʿmal ṣāliḥan lā sayyiʾan, “do good, not evil”; bal: uṭlub ḥalālan bal ṭayyiban, “seek what is lawful, rather what is pure”; lākin: lā yaḥillu riyāʾun lākin ikhlāṣun, “showing off is not lawful, but sincerity is”. The fiqh of the examples is real: the order of the acts of prayer, the number of rakʿas of the forenoon prayer.

The emphasis (tawkīd), of two kinds: by repeating the word, uṭlubi al-ikhlāṣa al-ikhlāṣa, “seek sincerity, sincerity”; and by a word of emphasis, utruki al-dhunūba kullahā, “leave the sins, all of them”. The substitute (badal), in three kinds: the whole, uʿbud rabbaka ilāha al-ʿālamīna, “worship your Lord, the God of the worlds”; the part, ubghiḍu al-nāsa man ʿaṣā llāha taʿālā minhum, “I hate, of the people, those who disobey God”; inclusion, iḥfaẓi llāha taʿālā ḥaqqahu, “keep God's right”, literally “keep God, His right”.

The fifth follower, which the Ājurrūmiyya does not have, is the explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān): āmannā bi-nabiyyinā Muḥammadin, “we believe in our Prophet, Muḥammad”. Muḥammad follows nabiyyinā in jarr and makes it clear by the better-known name. It looks like the badal of the whole, and later books discuss how the two differ; for now it is enough that both follow their noun in every sign of iʿrāb.

terms.en: the adjective (the Ājurrūmiyya's naʿt)
the conjunction with one of the ten particles
the emphasis: by repetition, or by kull and its like
the substitute: of the whole, the part, inclusion
the explanatory apposition: a clearer name

examples.en: uʿbudi llāha al-ʿaẓīma, “worship God the Mighty”: the adjective
yajibu al-ʿilmu thumma al-ʿamalu, “knowledge is a duty, then action”: ʿaṭf with thumma
utruki al-dhunūba kullahā, “leave the sins, all of them”: the emphasis
iḥfaẓi llāha taʿālā ḥaqqahu, “keep God's right”: the badal of inclusion
āmannā bi-nabiyyinā Muḥammadin, “we believe in our Prophet, Muḥammad”: the explanatory apposition

tasks.prompt: Name the follower and the word it follows: uṭīʿu llāha wa-l-rasūla; uṭlubi al-ikhlāṣa al-ikhlāṣa; uʿbud rabbaka ilāha al-ʿālamīna.
tasks.arabic: أُطِيعُ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ — اطْلُبِ الْإِخْلَاصَ الْإِخْلَاصَ — اعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ إِلَهَ الْعَالَمِينَ
tasks.answer: Al-rasūla: joined by wa- to llāha, in naṣb. The second al-ikhlāṣa: emphasis by repetition of the first, in naṣb. Ilāha: badal of the whole from rabbaka, in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: What is the badal in ubghiḍu al-nāsa man ʿaṣā llāha taʿālā minhum, and of which kind?
tasks.arabic: أُبْغِضُ النَّاسَ مَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ تَعَالَى مِنْهُمْ
tasks.answer: Man ʿaṣā llāha minhum, “those of them who disobey God”, is a badal of the part from al-nāsa; minhum ties it back to the people. As a word with a fixed ending, man stands in the place of naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Give the meaning of the particle in: ṣalli al-ḍuḥā arbaʿan aw thamāniyan; uṭlub ḥalālan bal ṭayyiban; iʿmal ṣāliḥan lā sayyiʾan.
tasks.arabic: صَلِّ الضُّحَى أَرْبَعًا أَوْ ثَمَانِيًا — اطْلُبْ حَلَالًا بَلْ طَيِّبًا — اعْمَلْ صَالِحًا لَا سَيِّئًا
tasks.answer: Aw: choice, “four or eight”. Bal: turning to something better, “rather what is pure”. Lā: denying of the second what is said of the first, “good, not evil”.

tasks.prompt: Which follower does Birgivī have that the Ājurrūmiyya lacks? Give his example and explain it.
tasks.answer: The explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān): āmannā bi-nabiyyinā Muḥammadin. Muḥammadin follows nabiyyinā in jarr and makes it clear by the better-known name.

quiz.prompt: How many followers does Birgivī count?
quiz.explanation: He adds the explanatory apposition to the four of the Ājurrūmiyya.

quiz.prompt: In uṭlubi al-ikhlāṣa al-ikhlāṣa, the second al-ikhlāṣa is…
quiz.explanation: The word itself is repeated.

quiz.prompt: Iḥfaẓi llāha ḥaqqahu has a badal of…
quiz.explanation: God's right belongs to Him: ishtimāl.

quiz.prompt: In āmannā bi-nabiyyinā Muḥammadin, Muḥammadin is…
quiz.explanation: It follows nabiyyinā and makes it clear.

quiz.prompt: Which particle gives order with a delay in yajibu al-ʿilmu thumma al-ʿamalu?
quiz.explanation: Knowledge first, then action.

quiz.prompt: A-riḍāʾa llāhi taṭlubu am sakhaṭahu? uses am to…
quiz.explanation: After the hamza of the question: “this or that?”.

quiz.prompt: How do the followers get their iʿrāb?
quiz.explanation: They are governed by following (bi-l-tabaʿiyya).

text.original: وَالضَّرْبُ الثَّانِي خَمْسَةٌ: الْأَوَّلُ الصِّفَةُ، نَحْوُ: اعْبُدِ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ. وَالثَّانِي الْعَطْفُ بِأَحَدِ الْحُرُوفِ الْعَشَرَةِ: الْوَاوِ، نَحْوُ: أُطِيعُ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ، وَالْفَاءِ، نَحْوُ: تَجِبُ تَكْبِيرَةُ الِافْتِتَاحِ فَالْقِيَامُ، وَثُمَّ، نَحْوُ: يَجِبُ الْعِلْمُ ثُمَّ الْعَمَلُ، وَحَتَّى، نَحْوُ: مَاتَ النَّاسُ حَتَّى الْأَنْبِيَاءُ عَلَيْهِمُ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ، وَأَوْ، نَحْوُ: صَلِّ الضُّحَى أَرْبَعًا أَوْ ثَمَانِيًا، وَإِمَّا، نَحْوُ: اعْمَلْ إِمَّا وَاجِبًا وَإِمَّا مُسْتَحَبًّا، وَأَمْ، نَحْوُ: أَرِضَاءَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى تَطْلُبُ أَمْ سَخَطَهُ، وَلَا، نَحْوُ: اعْمَلْ صَالِحًا لَا سَيِّئًا، وَبَلْ، نَحْوُ: اطْلُبْ حَلَالًا بَلْ طَيِّبًا، وَلَكِنْ، نَحْوُ: لَا يَحِلُّ رِيَاءٌ لَكِنْ إِخْلَاصٌ.
text.en: The second kind is five. The first is the adjective (ṣifa), as uʿbudi Allāha al-ʿaẓīma “worship God, the Mighty”. The second is the conjunction (ʿaṭf) with one of the ten particles: wa-, as uṭīʿu Allāha wa-al-rasūla “I obey God and the Messenger”; fa-, as tajibu takbīratu al-iftitāḥi fa-al-qiyāmu “the opening takbīr is binding, and then the standing”; thumma, as yajibu al-ʿilmu thumma al-ʿamalu “knowledge is binding, then action”; ḥattā, as māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu ʿalayhimu al-ṣalātu wa-al-salāmu “the people died, even the prophets, upon them be blessing and peace”; aw, as ṣalli al-ḍuḥā arbaʿan aw thamāniyan “pray the forenoon prayer, four or eight [rakʿas]”; immā, as iʿmal immā wājiban wa-immā mustaḥabban “do either what is obligatory or what is recommended”; am, as a-riḍāʾa Allāhi taʿālā taṭlubu am sakhaṭahu “is it the good pleasure of God Most High you seek, or His anger?”; lā, as iʿmal ṣāliḥan lā sayyiʾan “do good, not evil”; bal, as uṭlub ḥalālan bal ṭayyiban “seek what is lawful, nay, what is pure”; and lākin, as lā yaḥillu riyāʾun lākin ikhlāṣun “showing off is not lawful, but sincerity [is]”.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ التَّأْكِيدُ، نَحْوُ: اطْلُبِ الْإِخْلَاصَ الْإِخْلَاصَ، وَنَحْوُ: اتْرُكِ الذُّنُوبَ كُلَّهَا. وَالرَّابِعُ الْبَدَلُ، نَحْوُ: اعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ إِلَهَ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَنَحْوُ: أُبْغِضُ النَّاسَ مَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ تَعَالَى مِنْهُمْ، وَنَحْوُ: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى حَقَّهُ. وَالْخَامِسُ عَطْفُ الْبَيَانِ، نَحْوُ: آمَنَّا بِنَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ.
text.en: The third is the emphasis (taʾkīd), as uṭlubi al-ikhlāṣa al-ikhlāṣa “seek sincerity, sincerity”, and as utruki al-dhunūba kullahā “leave sins, all of them”. The fourth is the substitute (badal), as uʿbud rabbaka ilāha al-ʿālamīna “worship your Lord, the God of the worlds”, and as ubghiḍu al-nāsa man ʿaṣā Allāha taʿālā minhum “I hate the people, those of them who disobey God Most High”, and as iḥfaẓi Allāha taʿālā ḥaqqahu “keep God Most High, His right”. The fifth is the explicative apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān), as āmannā bi-nabiyyinā Muḥammadin ʿalayhi al-ṣalātu wa-al-salāmu “we believe in our Prophet Muḥammad, upon him be blessing and peace”.

lessons.title: The ten signs and the nine kinds
body: The third chapter gives the last ten of the hundred: the signs of iʿrāb. “It is a vowel, or a letter, or a dropping.” Three vowels: ḍamma, fatḥa, kasra. Four letters: wāw, yāʾ, alif, nūn. Three droppings, which belong to the verb only: the dropping of the vowel, the dropping of the last letter, and the dropping of the nūn. Ten in all.

Notice where the sukūn has gone. The Ājurrūmiyya counted it as a sign of jazm beside the vowels; Birgivī calls it “the dropping of the vowel”: lam yaḍrib is yaḍribu with its ḍamma taken away. In the same way the dropping of the last letter is the jazm of a weak verb, and the dropping of the nūn the naṣb and jazm of the five verbs.

Then the inflected words are sorted by the signs they take into nine kinds, in four groups. By vowels alone, and by letters alone: these two belong to the noun. By vowels with a dropping, and by letters with a dropping: these two belong to the verb. The next four lessons take the groups one by one.

Two terms run through them. A kind is “complete in iʿrāb” (tāmm al-iʿrāb) when it has a different sign for each of its states, and “incomplete” (nāqiṣ al-iʿrāb) when two of its states share one sign. The singular noun is complete: Zaydun, Zaydan, Zaydin. The dual is incomplete: al-Zaydayni serves naṣb and jarr.

terms.en: a vowel: ḍamma, fatḥa, kasra
here: a letter as sign: wāw, yāʾ, alif, nūn
a dropping: of the vowel, the last letter, the nūn
complete in iʿrāb: a different sign for each state
incomplete in iʿrāb: two states share a sign

examples.en: ḍammatun, fatḥatun, kasratun: the three vowels
wāwun, yāʾun, alifun, nūnun: the four letters

examples.arabic: حَذْفُ الْحَرَكَةِ، وَحَذْفُ الْآخِرِ، وَحَذْفُ النُّونِ
examples.en: the three droppings, of the verb only

tasks.prompt: Name the sign of iʿrāb in Birgivī's terms: lam yaḍrib; al-muslimūna; lam yaḍribū; kitābun.
tasks.arabic: لَمْ يَضْرِبْ — الْمُسْلِمُونَ — لَمْ يَضْرِبُوا — كِتَابٌ
tasks.answer: Lam yaḍrib: the dropping of the vowel. Al-muslimūna: the letter wāw. Lam yaḍribū: the dropping of the nūn. Kitābun: the vowel ḍamma.

tasks.prompt: Why does Birgivī not count the sukūn among the signs, and how does he name it?
tasks.answer: For him the sukūn of jazm is not a sign added but a vowel taken away: “the dropping of the vowel”, one of the three droppings, which belong to the verb only.

tasks.prompt: Which groups of inflected words belong to the noun and which to the verb?
tasks.answer: By vowels alone and by letters alone: the noun. By vowels with a dropping and by letters with a dropping: the verb.

tasks.prompt: Is the sound masculine plural complete or incomplete in iʿrāb? Explain.
tasks.answer: Incomplete: it has only two signs for three states (wāw in rafʿ, yāʾ in both naṣb and jarr).

quiz.prompt: How many signs of iʿrāb does Birgivī count?
quiz.explanation: Three vowels, four letters, three droppings.

quiz.prompt: What does Birgivī call the sukūn of jazm?
quiz.explanation: Lam yaḍrib: yaḍribu with its ḍamma taken away.

quiz.prompt: To which do the three droppings belong?
quiz.explanation: Vowel, last letter and nūn are dropped in verbs.

quiz.prompt: How many kinds of inflected word are there?
quiz.explanation: In four groups, by the signs they take.

quiz.prompt: What does “complete in iʿrāb” (tāmm) mean?
options: A different sign for each state
quiz.explanation: Zaydun, Zaydan, Zaydin.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is incomplete in iʿrāb?
quiz.explanation: Its yāʾ serves naṣb and jarr.

quiz.prompt: Which are the four letters of iʿrāb?
quiz.explanation: Hamza, nūn, yāʾ, tāʾ are the prefixes of anaytu, not signs of iʿrāb.

text.original: وَهُوَ إِمَّا حَرَكَةٌ أَوْ حَرْفٌ أَوْ حَذْفٌ. وَالْحَرَكَةُ ثَلَاثَةٌ: ضَمَّةٌ وَفَتْحَةٌ وَكَسْرَةٌ. وَالْحَرْفُ أَرْبَعَةٌ: وَاوٌ وَيَاءٌ وَأَلِفٌ وَنُونٌ. وَالْحَذْفُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِالْفِعْلِ: حَذْفُ الْحَرَكَةِ، وَحَذْفُ الْآخِرِ، وَحَذْفُ النُّونِ. فَالْجُمْلَةُ عَشَرَةٌ.
text.en: It is either a vowel, a letter or a dropping. The vowels are three: ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra. The letters are four: wāw, yāʾ, alif and nūn. The droppings are three, and belong to the verb only: dropping the vowel, dropping the last letter and dropping the nūn. So in all they are ten.

text.original: وَأَنْوَاعُ الْمُعْرَبِ بِالْقِيَاسِ إِلَى مَا أُعْطِيَ لَهَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْعَشَرَةِ تِسْعَةٌ؛ لِأَنَّ إِعْرَابَهَا إِمَّا بِالْحَرَكَةِ الْمَحْضَةِ أَوْ بِالْحُرُوفِ الْمَحْضَةِ، وَهُمَا مُخْتَصَّانِ بِالِاسْمِ، أَوْ بِالْحَرَكَةِ مَعَ الْحَذْفِ أَوْ بِالْحُرُوفِ مَعَ الْحَذْفِ، وَهُمَا مُخْتَصَّانِ بِالْفِعْلِ.
text.en: The kinds of inflected word, measured by what is given to them of these ten, are nine; for their iʿrāb is either by vowels alone or by letters alone, and these two belong to the noun only, or by vowels with dropping or by letters with dropping, and these two belong to the verb only.

lessons.title: Nouns inflected by vowels
body: The first group, inflected by vowels alone, has three kinds. One is complete in iʿrāb: ḍamma in rafʿ, fatḥa in naṣb, kasra in jarr. It is the declinable singular and the declinable broken plural: jāʾanā al-rasūlu, ṣaddaqnā al-rasūla, āmannā bi-l-rasūli, “the Messenger came to us, we believed him, we believe in him”; nazala min al-samāʾi kutubun, ṣaddaqnā al-kutuba, āmannā bi-l-kutubi, “books came down from heaven, we believed the books, we believe in the books”.

Two are incomplete. The diptote (ghayr al-munṣarif) has the ḍamma in rafʿ and the fatḥa in both naṣb and jarr: jāʾanā Aḥmadu, ṣaddaqnā Aḥmada, āmannā bi-Aḥmada. The sound feminine plural has the ḍamma in rafʿ and the kasra in both naṣb and jarr: jāʾanā muʿjizātun, ṣaddaqnā muʿjizātin, āmannā bi-muʿjizātin, “miracles came to us, we believed in miracles”.

The examples are built as a set: every kind is shown with the same three verbs, jāʾanā (rafʿ: the doer), ṣaddaqnā (naṣb: the object) and āmannā bi- (jarr: after the particle). The pattern makes the signs leap out, and the creed is in the words: the Messenger, the books, the Prophet Aḥmad, the miracles.

This is the Ājurrūmiyya's chapter of the words inflected by vowels and its exceptions, said in other words. What the Ājurrūmiyya called the two exceptions (the diptote in khafḍ, the feminine plural in naṣb), Birgivī calls the two incomplete kinds, because in each two states share one sign.

terms.en: the declinable singular: complete in iʿrāb
the broken plural
the diptote: fatḥa in naṣb and jarr
the sound feminine plural: kasra in naṣb and jarr

examples.arabic: جَاءَنَا الرَّسُولُ — صَدَّقْنَا الرَّسُولَ — آمَنَّا بِالرَّسُولِ
examples.en: the declinable singular: ḍamma, fatḥa, kasra

examples.arabic: جَاءَنَا أَحْمَدُ — صَدَّقْنَا أَحْمَدَ — آمَنَّا بِأَحْمَدَ
examples.en: the diptote: fatḥa in naṣb and in jarr

examples.arabic: جَاءَنَا مُعْجِزَاتٌ — صَدَّقْنَا مُعْجِزَاتٍ — آمَنَّا بِمُعْجِزَاتٍ
examples.en: the sound feminine plural: kasra in naṣb and in jarr

tasks.prompt: Put kutubun through Birgivī's three verbs (jāʾanā, ṣaddaqnā, āmannā bi-), without the article, and name the signs.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanā kutubun (ḍamma), ṣaddaqnā kutuban (fatḥa), āmannā bi-kutubin (kasra). The broken plural is complete in iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Why is the diptote incomplete in iʿrāb? Show it on Aḥmad.
tasks.answer: Two of its states share one sign: Aḥmadu in rafʿ, but Aḥmada in both naṣb and jarr (ṣaddaqnā Aḥmada, āmannā bi-Aḥmada).

tasks.prompt: In ṣaddaqnā muʿjizātin, why is muʿjizātin in naṣb though it ends in a kasra?
tasks.arabic: صَدَّقْنَا مُعْجِزَاتٍ
tasks.answer: It is the object of ṣaddaqnā. The sound feminine plural takes the kasra in naṣb as in jarr; that is why it is incomplete in iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: What does the Ājurrūmiyya call what Birgivī calls the two incomplete kinds of this group?
tasks.answer: The exceptions to the words inflected by vowels: the sound feminine plural in naṣb by the kasra, and the noun that is not declinable in khafḍ by the fatḥa.

quiz.prompt: Which nouns are complete in iʿrāb by vowels?
options: The diptote and the feminine plural
The declinable singular and the declinable broken plural
quiz.explanation: Ḍamma, fatḥa, kasra: one sign for each state.

quiz.prompt: Āmannā bi-Aḥmada: what is the sign of jarr?
quiz.explanation: The diptote takes the fatḥa in jarr.

quiz.prompt: Ṣaddaqnā muʿjizātin: the sign of naṣb is…
quiz.explanation: The sound feminine plural.

quiz.prompt: Why are Birgivī's examples built on jāʾanā, ṣaddaqnā and āmannā bi-?
options: They are the only verbs he knows
They show each kind in rafʿ, naṣb and jarr side by side
quiz.explanation: Doer, object, and noun after a particle.

quiz.prompt: How many kinds are in the group inflected by vowels?
quiz.explanation: Singular and broken plural count as one complete kind.

quiz.prompt: Al-kutuba in ṣaddaqnā al-kutuba is…
quiz.explanation: The broken plural is complete in iʿrāb.

quiz.prompt: What does the Ājurrūmiyya call the feminine plural's kasra in naṣb?
options: An exception to the rule of the vowels
quiz.explanation: Birgivī names it incomplete iʿrāb.

text.original: وَالْأَوَّلُ إِمَّا تَامُّ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ أَنْ يَكُونَ رَفْعُهُ بِالضَّمَّةِ وَنَصْبُهُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْكَسْرَةِ، وَذَلِكَ الْمُفْرَدُ الْمُنْصَرِفُ وَالْجَمْعُ الْمُكَسَّرُ الْمُنْصَرِفُ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَصَدَّقْنَا الرَّسُولَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَآمَنَّا بِالرَّسُولِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَنَحْوُ: نَزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ كُتُبٌ، وَصَدَّقْنَا الْكُتُبَ، وَآمَنَّا بِالْكُتُبِ.
text.en: The first is either of complete iʿrāb (tāmm al-iʿrāb), that is, its rafʿ is by the ḍamma, its naṣb by the fatḥa and its jarr by the kasra; that is the singular that takes tanwīn and the broken plural that takes tanwīn, as jāʾanā al-rasūlu ʿalayhi al-salāmu “the Messenger, upon him be peace, came to us”, wa-ṣaddaqnā al-rasūla ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed the Messenger, upon him be peace”, wa-āmannā bi-al-rasūli ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed in the Messenger, upon him be peace”; and as nazala mina al-samāʾi kutubun “books came down from heaven”, wa-ṣaddaqnā al-kutuba “and we believed the books”, wa-āmannā bi-al-kutubi “and we believed in the books”.

text.original: وَإِمَّا نَاقِصُ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: قِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالضَّمَّةِ وَنَصْبُهُ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ، وَذَلِكَ غَيْرُ الْمُنْصَرِفِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا أَحْمَدُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَصَدَّقْنَا أَحْمَدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَآمَنَّا بِأَحْمَدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ. وَقِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالضَّمَّةِ وَنَصْبُهُ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْكَسْرَةِ، وَذَلِكَ جَمْعُ الْمُؤَنَّثِ السَّالِمِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا مُعْجِزَاتٌ، وَصَدَّقْنَا مُعْجِزَاتٍ، وَآمَنَّا بِمُعْجِزَاتٍ.
text.en: Or it is of incomplete iʿrāb (nāqiṣ al-iʿrāb), and that is of two divisions. A division whose rafʿ is by the ḍamma and whose naṣb and jarr are by the fatḥa; that is the diptote (ghayr al-munṣarif), as jāʾanā Aḥmadu ʿalayhi al-salāmu “Aḥmad, upon him be peace, came to us”, wa-ṣaddaqnā Aḥmada ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed Aḥmad, upon him be peace”, wa-āmannā bi-Aḥmada ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed in Aḥmad, upon him be peace”. And a division whose rafʿ is by the ḍamma and whose naṣb and jarr are by the kasra; that is the sound feminine plural, as jāʾanā muʿjizātun “miracles came to us”, wa-ṣaddaqnā muʿjizātin “and we believed miracles”, wa-āmannā bi-muʿjizātin “and we believed in miracles”.

lessons.title: Nouns inflected by letters
body: The second group, inflected by letters alone, again has one complete kind and two incomplete. The complete kind is the six nouns: wāw in rafʿ, alif in naṣb, yāʾ in jarr. They are abūhu (his father), akhūhu (his brother), ḥamūhā (her in-law), hanūhu (his thing), fūhu (his mouth) and dhū mālin (one with wealth): jāʾanā Abū al-Qāsimi, ṣaddaqnā Abā al-Qāsimi, āmannā bi-Abī al-Qāsimi, “Abū al-Qāsim came to us, we believed him, we believe in him”, Abū al-Qāsim being the Prophet's kunya.

Birgivī counts six where the Ājurrūmiyya counted five: he adds han, “a thing” (used for something one does not name). And he gives the conditions the Ājurrūmiyya only showed: the noun must be joined to a word other than the yāʾ of the speaker (abī, “my father”, does not count), singular (not abawāni), and not a diminutive (not ubayy).

The first incomplete kind has the wāw in rafʿ and the yāʾ in naṣb and jarr: the sound masculine plural, and with it ūlū, “possessors”, and ʿishrūna and its sisters, the tens from twenty to ninety: jāʾanā al-mursalūna, ṣaddaqnā al-mursalīna, āmannā bi-l-mursalīna, “the messengers came to us…”.

The second incomplete kind has the alif in rafʿ and the yāʾ in naṣb and jarr: the dual, and with it ithnāni, “two”, and kilā, “both”, when joined to a pronoun: jāʾanā al-ithnāni kilāhumā, ay al-kitābu wa-l-sunnatu, “the two came to us, both of them, that is, the Book and the Sunna”; ittabaʿnā al-ithnayni kilayhimā, ʿamilnā bi-l-ithnayni kilayhimā. Kilā joined to a visible noun keeps its alif (kilā al-rajulayni); only with a pronoun does it change.
So the words that look like plurals or duals but are not (ūlū, ʿishrūna, ithnāni, kilāhumā) are inflected as if they were. The madrasa calls them “attached” to the plural and the dual.

terms.en: the six nouns: wāw, alif, yāʾ
not a diminutive: a condition of the six nouns
possessors: inflected like the sound plural
the tens, inflected like the sound plural
both: like the dual when joined to a pronoun

examples.arabic: جَاءَنَا أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ — صَدَّقْنَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ — آمَنَّا بِأَبِي الْقَاسِمِ
examples.en: one of the six nouns: wāw, alif, yāʾ
the sound masculine plural: wāw in rafʿ, yāʾ in naṣb and jarr
al-ithnāni kilāhumā, “the two, both of them”: like the dual
ittabaʿnā al-ithnayni kilayhimā: the yāʾ in naṣb

tasks.prompt: Put dhū mālin through the three states with jāʾanā, ṣaddaqnā and āmannā bi-.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanā dhū mālin; ṣaddaqnā dhā mālin; āmannā bi-dhī mālin: wāw, alif, yāʾ.

tasks.prompt: Give the three conditions for the six nouns to take letters, and an example that fails each.
tasks.answer: Joined to a word other than the yāʾ of the speaker (abī, “my father”, fails); singular (abawāni, “two fathers”, fails); not a diminutive (ubayy, “little father”, fails).

tasks.prompt: Why is ʿishrūna inflected like al-muslimūna, and kilāhumā like al-Zaydāni?
tasks.answer: They are attached to the plural and the dual: ʿishrūna and its sisters, and ūlū, take wāw and yāʾ like the sound masculine plural; ithnāni, and kilā joined to a pronoun, take alif and yāʾ like the dual.

tasks.prompt: Which noun does Birgivī add to the Ājurrūmiyya's five?
tasks.answer: Han (hanūhu), “a thing”, used for something one does not name.

quiz.prompt: How many nouns does Birgivī count where the Ājurrūmiyya counted five?
quiz.explanation: He adds han.

quiz.prompt: Āmannā bi-Abī al-Qāsimi: the sign of jarr is…
quiz.explanation: The six nouns: wāw, alif, yāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is inflected like the sound masculine plural?
quiz.explanation: ʿIshrūna and its sisters, and ūlū.

quiz.prompt: When is kilā inflected like the dual?
options: When joined to a visible noun
quiz.explanation: Kilāhumā, kilayhimā.

quiz.prompt: Which fails the conditions of the six nouns?
quiz.explanation: Joined to the yāʾ of the speaker, it does not take the letters.

quiz.prompt: Ṣaddaqnā al-mursalīna: the sign of naṣb is…
quiz.explanation: The sound masculine plural shares the yāʾ between naṣb and jarr.

quiz.prompt: Which kind of this group is complete in iʿrāb?
quiz.explanation: Each of its states has its own letter.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي إِمَّا تَامُّ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ أَنْ يَكُونَ رَفْعُهُ بِالْوَاوِ وَنَصْبُهُ بِالْأَلِفِ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْيَاءِ، وَذَلِكَ الْأَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةُ الْمُعْتَلَّةُ الْمُضَافَةُ إِلَى غَيْرِ يَاءِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ مُفْرَدَةً مُكَبَّرَةً، وَهِيَ: أَبُوهُ، وَأَخُوهُ، وَحَمُوهَا، وَهَنُوهُ، وَفُوهُ، وَذُو مَالٍ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَصَدَّقْنَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَآمَنَّا بِأَبِي الْقَاسِمِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ.
text.en: The second is either of complete iʿrāb, that is, its rafʿ is by the wāw, its naṣb by the alif and its jarr by the yāʾ; that is the six weak nouns, joined in iḍāfa to something other than the yāʾ of the first person, singular and not diminutive. They are: abūhu “his father”, akhūhu “his brother”, ḥamūhā “her father-in-law”, hanūhu “his thing”, fūhu “his mouth” and dhū mālin “possessor of wealth”; as jāʾanā abū al-Qāsimi ʿalayhi al-salāmu “Abū al-Qāsim, upon him be peace, came to us”, wa-ṣaddaqnā abā al-Qāsimi ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed Abū al-Qāsim, upon him be peace”, wa-āmannā bi-abī al-Qāsimi ʿalayhi al-salāmu “and we believed in Abū al-Qāsim, upon him be peace”.

text.original: وَإِمَّا نَاقِصُ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: قِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالْوَاوِ وَنَصْبُهُ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْيَاءِ، وَذَلِكَ جَمْعُ الْمُذَكَّرِ السَّالِمِ وَأُولُو وَعِشْرُونَ وَأَخَوَاتُهَا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ، وَصَدَّقْنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ، وَآمَنَّا بِالْمُرْسَلِينَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ.
text.en: Or it is of incomplete iʿrāb, and that is of two divisions. A division whose rafʿ is by the wāw and whose naṣb and jarr are by the yāʾ; that is the sound masculine plural, ūlū “possessors of” and ʿishrūna “twenty” and its sisters, as jāʾanā al-mursalūna ʿalayhimu al-salāmu “the messengers, upon them be peace, came to us”, wa-ṣaddaqnā al-mursalīna ʿalayhimu al-salāmu “and we believed the messengers, upon them be peace”, wa-āmannā bi-al-mursalīna ʿalayhimu al-salāmu “and we believed in the messengers, upon them be peace”.

text.original: وَقِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالْأَلِفِ وَنَصْبُهُ وَجَرُّهُ بِالْيَاءِ، وَذَلِكَ التَّثْنِيَةُ وَاثْنَانِ وَكِلَا مُضَافًا إِلَى مُضْمَرٍ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنَا الِاثْنَانِ كِلَاهُمَا، أَيِ الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ، وَاتَّبَعْنَا الِاثْنَيْنِ كِلَيْهِمَا، وَعَمِلْنَا بِالِاثْنَيْنِ كِلَيْهِمَا.
text.en: And a division whose rafʿ is by the alif and whose naṣb and jarr are by the yāʾ; that is the dual, ithnāni “two”, and kilā “both” joined in iḍāfa to a pronoun, as jāʾanā al-ithnāni kilāhumā “the two came to us, both of them”, that is, the Book and the Sunna; wa-ittabaʿnā al-ithnayni kilayhimā “and we followed the two, both of them”; wa-ʿamilnā bi-al-ithnayni kilayhimā “and we acted on the two, both of them”.

lessons.title: The verb's iʿrāb
body: The third group, inflected by a vowel with a dropping, belongs to the verb and is always complete in iʿrāb, for the verb has three states and a different sign in each. It has two kinds. The present verb with no pronoun attached, whose last letter is sound: ḍamma in rafʿ, fatḥa in naṣb, and in jazm the dropping of the vowel: nuḥibbu an nashfaʿa wa-lam nuḥram, “we love to intercede, and we were not deprived”. Nuḥibbu in rafʿ, nashfaʿa in naṣb after an, nuḥram in jazm after lam.

The present verb with no pronoun attached, whose last letter is weak: in jazm the dropping of the last letter: nadʿū llāha taʿālā an yaʿfuwanā wa-lam yarminā fī al-nāri, “we pray to God that He pardon us; and He has not cast us into the Fire”. Nadʿū in rafʿ, its ḍamma assumed on the wāw; yaʿfuwa in naṣb after an, the fatḥa seen on the wāw; yarmi in jazm after lam, its yāʾ dropped.

The fourth group, inflected by a letter with a dropping, is always incomplete in iʿrāb: the present verb with a pronoun attached other than the nūn, the five verbs of the Ājurrūmiyya. Rafʿ by the nūn, naṣb and jazm by dropping it: al-awliyāʾu wa-l-ʿulamāʾu yashfaʿāni yawma al-qiyāmati, fa-narjū an yashfaʿā lanā wa-lam yuʿriḍā ʿannā, “the friends of God and the scholars intercede on the Day of Rising; so we hope that they intercede for us and do not turn away from us”.

“Other than the nūn” keeps out the nūn of the women, yaḍribna, whose ending is fixed and which is therefore not inflected at all. And notice the dual yashfaʿāni after two plural subjects: the two kinds of people, the friends of God and the scholars, are treated as two.
Count the kinds now: three by vowels, three by letters, two by a vowel with a dropping, one by a letter with a dropping: nine, as the chapter promised.

terms.en: the dropping of the vowel: jazm of the sound verb
the dropping of the last letter: jazm of the weak verb
a weak letter: wāw, yāʾ, alif
the present with a pronoun other than the nūn

examples.en: nuḥibbu an nashfaʿa wa-lam nuḥram: one verb in rafʿ, naṣb and jazm
an yaʿfuwanā wa-lam yarminā: the weak verb in naṣb, and in jazm by dropping its yāʾ
yashfaʿāni, an yashfaʿā, lam yuʿriḍā: the nūn kept, then dropped

tasks.prompt: Give the state and the sign of each verb in nuḥibbu an nashfaʿa wa-lam nuḥram.
tasks.arabic: نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَشْفَعَ وَلَمْ نُحْرَمْ
tasks.answer: Nuḥibbu: rafʿ by the ḍamma (no governor of naṣb or jazm). Nashfaʿa: naṣb by the fatḥa, after an. Nuḥram: jazm by the dropping of the vowel, after lam (a passive verb).

tasks.prompt: In nadʿū llāha … an yaʿfuwanā wa-lam yarminā, why is the ḍamma of nadʿū not heard, while the fatḥa of yaʿfuwa is?
tasks.arabic: نَدْعُو — أَنْ يَعْفُوَنَا
tasks.answer: A ḍamma on a final wāw is heavy, so in rafʿ it is assumed, not said (nadʿū). The fatḥa is light and is said on the wāw (yaʿfuwa). In jazm the weak letter itself is dropped (yarmi).

tasks.prompt: Put yashfaʿāni after lan and after lam, and name the signs.
tasks.arabic: يَشْفَعَانِ
tasks.answer: Lan yashfaʿā; lam yashfaʿā. In both the nūn is dropped: naṣb and jazm share one sign, so the five verbs are incomplete in iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Count the nine kinds of inflected word by their groups.
tasks.answer: By vowels: declinable singular and broken plural (complete), diptote, sound feminine plural (3). By letters: the six nouns (complete), sound masculine plural with its attached, dual with its attached (3). By a vowel with a dropping: sound-final present, weak-final present (2). By a letter with a dropping: the five verbs (1).

quiz.prompt: How is the sound-final present verb in jazm, in Birgivī's terms?
options: By the sukūn as a fourth vowel
By the dropping of the vowel
By the dropping of the nūn
quiz.explanation: Lam nuḥram.

quiz.prompt: How is the weak-final present verb in jazm?
quiz.explanation: Lam yarminā: the yāʾ of yarmī is dropped.

quiz.prompt: In nadʿū, “we pray”, the ḍamma of rafʿ is…
quiz.explanation: A ḍamma on a final wāw is too heavy to say.

quiz.prompt: Is the group “by a vowel with a dropping” complete or incomplete in iʿrāb?
quiz.explanation: Three states, three different signs.

quiz.prompt: Which verb is in the fourth group?
quiz.explanation: The present with a pronoun other than the nūn; yaḍribna has a fixed ending.

quiz.prompt: Why is yashfaʿāni dual after al-awliyāʾu wa-l-ʿulamāʾu?
options: The two kinds of people are treated as two
quiz.explanation: The friends of God and the scholars: two groups.

quiz.prompt: In an yashfaʿā lanā, the sign of naṣb is…
quiz.explanation: The five verbs share one sign between naṣb and jazm.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا تَامَّ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ قِسْمَانِ: قِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالضَّمَّةِ وَنَصْبُهُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ وَجَزْمُهُ بِحَذْفِ الْحَرَكَةِ، وَهُوَ الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّصِلْ بِآخِرِهِ ضَمِيرٌ وَهُوَ حَرْفٌ صَحِيحٌ، نَحْوُ: نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَشْفَعَ وَلَمْ نُحْرَمْ.
text.en: The third is only of complete iʿrāb, and it is of two divisions. A division whose rafʿ is by the ḍamma, its naṣb by the fatḥa and its jazm by dropping the vowel; that is the muḍāriʿ verb to whose end no pronoun is attached and whose last letter is a sound letter, as nuḥibbu an nashfaʿa wa-lam nuḥram “we love to intercede and not to be deprived”.

text.original: وَقِسْمٌ رَفْعُهُ بِالضَّمَّةِ وَنَصْبُهُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ وَجَزْمُهُ بِحَذْفِ الْآخِرِ، وَذَلِكَ الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّصِلْ بِآخِرِهِ ضَمِيرٌ وَهُوَ حَرْفُ عِلَّةٍ، نَحْوُ: نَدْعُو اللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَنْ يَعْفُوَنَا وَلَمْ يَرْمِنَا فِي النَّارِ.
text.en: And a division whose rafʿ is by the ḍamma, its naṣb by the fatḥa and its jazm by dropping the last letter; that is the muḍāriʿ verb to whose end no pronoun is attached and whose last letter is a weak letter, as nadʿū Allāha taʿālā an yaʿfuwanā wa-lam yarminā fī al-nāri “we pray God Most High to pardon us and not to cast us into the Fire”.

text.original: وَالرَّابِعُ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا نَاقِصَ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ الَّذِي اتَّصَلَ بِآخِرِهِ ضَمِيرٌ غَيْرُ النُّونِ، فَرَفْعُهُ بِالنُّونِ وَنَصْبُهُ وَجَزْمُهُ بِحَذْفِهَا، نَحْوُ: الْأَوْلِيَاءُ وَالْعُلَمَاءُ يَشْفَعَانِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، فَنَرْجُو أَنْ يَشْفَعَا لَنَا وَلَمْ يُعْرِضَا عَنَّا.
text.en: The fourth is only of incomplete iʿrāb: it is the muḍāriʿ verb to whose end a pronoun other than the nūn is attached; its rafʿ is by the nūn, and its naṣb and jazm by dropping it, as al-awliyāʾu wa-al-ʿulamāʾu yashfaʿāni yawma al-qiyāmati “the saints and the scholars will both intercede on the Day of Resurrection”, fa-narjū an yashfaʿā lanā wa-lam yuʿriḍā ʿannā “so we hope that they will intercede for us and not turn away from us”.

lessons.title: Heard, implied and by place
body: The book ends with one passage that sorts every iʿrāb into three. If the sign appears in the pronunciation it is heard (lafẓī), as in all the examples so far: al-rasūlu, al-rasūla, al-rasūli. If it does not appear but is supposed on the end of the word, it is implied (taqdīrī): anā al-ʿāṣī, “I am the disobedient one”, where al-ʿāṣī is the khabar in rafʿ, but its ḍamma is supposed on the yāʾ and not said.

If it neither appears nor is supposed on the end, it is by place (maḥallī): tawakkalnā ʿalā man lā yaʾtī al-khayru illā min jihatihi, “we have put our trust in Him from whom alone good comes”. Man, “the one who”, has a fixed ending; nothing on it changes or could change. Yet it stands where a noun in jarr stands, after ʿalā, and so it is said to be “in the place of jarr” (fī maḥall jarr).

The commentaries give the reason for the implied iʿrāb. On a final alif no vowel can be said at all (al-fatā, as the Ājurrūmiyya showed), so all three are implied there. On a final yāʾ or wāw the ḍamma and the kasra are heavy and are implied (al-ʿāṣī, nadʿū), but the fatḥa is light and is said: raʾaytu al-ʿāṣiya, an yaʿfuwa.

And the iʿrāb by place is what the madrasa says of every word with a fixed ending in a governed position: the pronouns (anā, “in the place of rafʿ”), the demonstratives, the relatives such as man and alladhī, and whole sentences that stand where a single word would. The student who has read the ʿAwāmil can now give, for every word of a sentence, its governor, its state, its sign, and whether that sign is heard, implied or by place.
On the Ottoman path the ʿAwāmil is followed by Birgivī's own Iẓhār al-asrār, which takes the same three chapters at greater length, and then by Ibn al-Ḥājib's Kāfiya with its commentary by Jāmī.

terms.en: heard iʿrāb: the sign is said
implied iʿrāb: the sign is supposed on the end
iʿrāb by place: a fixed word in a governed position
in the place of jarr

examples.en: anā al-ʿāṣī, “I am the disobedient one”: the ḍamma of al-ʿāṣī is implied

examples.arabic: تَوَكَّلْنَا عَلَى مَنْ لَا يَأْتِي الْخَيْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ جِهَتِهِ
examples.en: “we have put our trust in Him from whom alone good comes”: man is in the place of jarr

tasks.prompt: Heard, implied or by place? (a) al-rasūli in āmannā bi-l-rasūli; (b) al-ʿāṣī in anā al-ʿāṣī; (c) anā in anā al-ʿāṣī; (d) man in ʿalā man lā yaʾtī al-khayru.
tasks.arabic: آمَنَّا بِالرَّسُولِ — أَنَا الْعَاصِي — عَلَى مَنْ
tasks.answer: (a) Heard: the kasra is said. (b) Implied: the ḍamma is supposed on the yāʾ. (c) By place: anā is a pronoun with a fixed ending, in the place of rafʿ as mubtadaʾ. (d) By place: man has a fixed ending, in the place of jarr after ʿalā.

tasks.prompt: Why is the iʿrāb of al-ʿāṣī implied in rafʿ but heard in naṣb?
tasks.arabic: أَنَا الْعَاصِي — رَأَيْتُ الْعَاصِيَ
tasks.answer: A ḍamma on a final yāʾ is heavy and is not said, so it is supposed (anā al-ʿāṣī). A fatḥa is light and is said on the yāʾ (raʾaytu al-ʿāṣiya).

tasks.prompt: What is the difference between implied iʿrāb and iʿrāb by place?
tasks.answer: Implied iʿrāb is supposed on the end of a word that is inflected but cannot show its sign (al-ʿāṣī, al-fatā). Iʿrāb by place belongs to a word with a fixed ending, which never changes; only its position is in a state (man, anā).

text.original: ثُمَّ الْإِعْرَابُ إِنْ ظَهَرَ فِي اللَّفْظِ يُسَمَّى لَفْظِيًّا، كَمَا فِي الْأَمْثِلَةِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَظْهَرْ فِي اللَّفْظِ بَلْ قُدِّرَ فِي آخِرِهِ يُسَمَّى تَقْدِيرِيًّا، نَحْوُ: أَنَا الْعَاصِي، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَظْهَرْ وَلَمْ يُقَدَّرْ فِي آخِرِهِ يُسَمَّى مَحَلِّيًّا، نَحْوُ: تَوَكَّلْنَا عَلَى مَنْ لَا يَأْتِي الْخَيْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ جِهَتِهِ.
text.en: Then iʿrāb, if it appears in the pronunciation, is called audible (lafẓī), as in the examples mentioned; if it does not appear in the pronunciation but is supposed on the end [of the word], it is called implied (taqdīrī), as anā al-ʿāṣī “I am the disobedient one”; and if it neither appears nor is supposed on the end, it is called by place (maḥallī), as tawakkalnā ʿalā man lā yaʾtī al-khayru illā min jihatihi “we have put our trust in Him from whom alone good comes”.
